column1: # Quotation-mark glyph inventory — the closed set of Unicode characters that
# open or close a quoted span, used by the tokenizer's quoted-mention
# recognizer (Slice B, .notes/chat-fix-c-build-state.md) to collapse
# `OPEN word... CLOSE` into a single NP-typed token: quoting a bare content
# word is the syntactic device licensing an otherwise-N/verb-typed surface as
# a genuine referring expression (Quine 1940:26 via SEP "Quotation" §3.1: a
# mentioned/queried expression is a singular term).
# Source: Unicode Standard Annex #44 (Unicode Character Database), the
# General_Category property, as tabulated in the UCD's
# DerivedGeneralCategory.txt — verified against Unicode 18.0.0 (2026) by
# direct inspection of the primary data file
# (unicode-org/unicodetools:unicodetools/data/ucd/dev/extracted/
# DerivedGeneralCategory.txt), cross-checked against the UCD's
# Quotation_Mark property listing in PropList.txt for the ASCII pair.
# Two Unicode general categories carry the WHOLE loaded set:
#   Pi (Initial_Punctuation) — 12 members, opens a quoted span.
#   Pf (Final_Punctuation)   — 10 members, closes a quoted span.
# Ten of the 12 Pi members pair with exactly one Pf member (the `pairs_with`
# column carries that Pf member's code point); the remaining two Pi members
# (U+201B, U+201F) have no Pf counterpart in the UCD — real code points,
# genuinely unpaired, not a gap in this table.
# The two ASCII quote marks (U+0022 QUOTATION MARK, U+0027 APOSTROPHE) are
# General_Category Po (Other_Punctuation), NOT Pi/Pf — ASCII does not encode
# quote directionality — so they are role `ambiguous`: either glyph can open
# OR close a quoted span depending on position, and neither carries a
# `pairs_with` (any ambiguous glyph closes a span any ambiguous glyph opened).
# Format: `codepoint<TAB>glyph<TAB>role<TAB>pairs_with<TAB>name`
#   codepoint   4-6 hex digits, no "U+" prefix.
#   glyph       the literal UTF-8 character (for human sight-verification
#               against `codepoint`; the loader cross-checks the two agree).
#   role        initial | final | ambiguous
#   pairs_with  the paired glyph's hex codepoint, or the literal `-` if none.
#   name        the UCD character name, verbatim, for citation traceability.
codepoint
